make-qr.name: How to make a QR code
make-qr.blurb: Put a URL in, download a PNG, scan it with a phone before you print.
make-qr.title: How to make a QR code
make-qr.lead: A QR code is a door to one place. If the door is wrong, every poster is wrong. You will make one PNG in this tab and scan it before you print.
make-qr.result: A PNG that opens the right page on your phone, with a white margin, large enough to print.
make-qr.note: Use a full https URL. Do not encode a file. Host the file and encode the link. Open the QR tool when you have the URL.
make-qr.s1t: Decide what the code should open
make-qr.s1b: A page, a menu, a payment link: encode the https URL. A Wi-Fi name or table number can be plain text. Do not paste a file path. If the destination might change, encode a short URL you control.
make-qr.s2t: Open the QR tool and paste the URL
make-qr.s2b: Open the QR generator on cv.cm. Paste the full address, including https://. If you omit the scheme, some cameras search the words instead of opening the site. Check the preview still shows your text.
make-qr.s3t: Look at contrast and quiet zone
make-qr.s3b: Dark modules on a light ground scan more reliably. Leave a white margin around the square — that quiet zone is part of the code. Do not put the code on a busy photo without a white pad.
make-qr.s4b: Download the PNG. Keep this file; do not screenshot the preview. A screenshot can add compression and crop the margin.
make-qr.s5t: Scan it with a phone before you print
make-qr.s5b: Open the camera 20–30 cm away. The page must load. If you get a search box, the URL was incomplete. If nothing happens, enlarge the code or add margin. Only then print or send.
make-qr.s6b: On paper, keep the square at least 2 cm wide, more if it will be read from a door. Scale uniformly. A stretched rectangle will fail. After printing, scan the paper once more.
make-qr.diagram1: Three destinations: a https URL, short text, or a file you must not encode.
make-qr.diagram2: Scan the PNG with a phone before any print run. The page must open.

make-barcode.name: How to make a barcode
make-barcode.blurb: Choose Code 128, 39, or EAN-13, download a PNG, scan with the reader you will use.
make-barcode.title: How to make a barcode
make-barcode.lead: A barcode identifies a thing. A QR code opens a link. Pick the symbology, type the digits, then scan with the gun at the desk — not only your phone.
make-barcode.result: A PNG your real scanner reads, with the right symbology and a check digit if it is EAN-13.
make-barcode.note: Open the barcode tool when you know whether this is inventory (Code 128) or a retail GTIN (EAN-13). Do not invent someone else's product number.
make-barcode.s1b: Code 128 holds letters and digits for tickets and bins. Code 39 suits older guns. EAN-13 is retail: 12 digits plus a check. A QR code is the wrong tool for a shelf label that a 1D scanner must read.
make-barcode.s2t: Open the barcode tool and type the value
make-barcode.s2b: Open the barcode generator on cv.cm. Choose the symbology first, then type. Spaces in EAN-13 will fail. For Code 128, keep internal IDs short enough to print.
make-barcode.s3t: For EAN-13, type 12 digits and let the check fill in
make-barcode.s3b: The thirteenth digit is a checksum. If a shop scanner rejects the label, the check is wrong or the prefix is not yours. Do not invent a GTIN you do not own.
make-barcode.s4b: Download the PNG. Do not screenshot the preview. Keep a white margin when you place it on packaging.
make-barcode.s5t: Scan with the gun you will actually use
make-barcode.s5b: Phone cameras often read Code 128. Warehouse guns may only read EAN-13 or Code 39. Test on the device at the counter. If it beeps but the POS shows the wrong SKU, you encoded the wrong digits.
make-barcode.s6t: Print at a width the gun can see
make-barcode.s6b: A 1D barcode needs more width than a QR code of the same story. Do not rotate it into a tiny corner. After printing, scan the paper.
make-barcode.diagram1: Three symbologies: Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13. QR is for links.
make-barcode.diagram2: EAN-13 is 12 digits plus a check. Do not invent a GTIN you do not own.

merge-pdf.name: How to merge PDF files
merge-pdf.blurb: Drop PDFs in order, download one file, reopen it and count the pages.
merge-pdf.title: How to merge PDF files
merge-pdf.lead: You will combine several PDFs into one file in this tab. The list order is the page order. Then you open the download and count.
merge-pdf.result: One PDF whose page count equals the sum of the sources, in the order you chose.
merge-pdf.note: Open the merge tool when the files are on disk. Password-locked PDFs often cannot join until you unlock them. Nothing is uploaded.
merge-pdf.s1t: Collect the files and check they open
merge-pdf.s1b: Open each source once. Note page counts. If a file asks for a password, unlock it first. Merge cannot invent pages from a locked file.
merge-pdf.s2b: Open merge PDF on cv.cm. This tab does the work. Closing it discards the list.
merge-pdf.s3t: Drop in order, then reorder if needed
merge-pdf.s3b: The first row becomes page 1. Drag to reorder. Empty pages in a source stay empty. If cover should be first, put Cover.pdf on top.
merge-pdf.s4b: Add the page counts you noted. If the tool shows fewer files than you dropped, one was rejected (often encryption).
merge-pdf.s5b: Download one file. Keep the sources until you have verified the merge.
merge-pdf.s6b: 3 + 2 + 4 should be 9. Skim the first page of each original block. If page 1 is wrong, the list was wrong — not the download.
merge-pdf.diagram1: The first row in the list becomes page 1.
merge-pdf.diagram2: Open the download and count. Do not send until you have opened it once.

compress-pdf.name: How to compress a PDF
compress-pdf.blurb: Match the email or form limit, recompress pages, then open a photo-heavy page.
compress-pdf.title: How to compress a PDF / reduce PDF size
compress-pdf.lead: A smaller file that nobody can read is not a success. You will check the limit, compress in this tab, then open a real page.
compress-pdf.result: A PDF under the limit whose photos and type still read at 100%.
compress-pdf.note: Open the compress tool when you know the cap (email 10–25 MB, some forms 2 MB). This page re-encodes pages as JPEG in the tab.
compress-pdf.s1b: Email is often 10–25 MB. A government form may want 2 MB. Look at the field, not a guess. Note the current file size too.
compress-pdf.s2b: Drop the PDF. Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the result.
compress-pdf.s3b: Pages are re-encoded. Text usually survives. Photos take the hit. Wait until the new size appears.
compress-pdf.s4t: Compare size against a real page
compress-pdf.s4b: If it is still over the cap, compress again or split. If a photo page is mushy, use milder compression — pick the largest file that still fits.
compress-pdf.s5b: Keep the original until you have opened the new file.
compress-pdf.s6b: If digits in a table smear, you overshot. Go back one quality step. A thumbnail can look fine while the full page does not.
compress-pdf.diagram1: Match email, form, or upload limits — they are not the same.
compress-pdf.diagram2: Pick the largest file that still fits. Then read a real page.

heic-to-jpg.name: How to convert HEIC to JPG
heic-to-jpg.blurb: iPhone photos are often HEIC. Export JPG in Safari or Chrome, then open the JPG on the PC you will send it to.
heic-to-jpg.title: How to convert HEIC to JPG
heic-to-jpg.lead: HEIC is smaller. JPG opens on Windows and in most chat apps. You will convert a copy in this tab and open the JPG once before sending.
heic-to-jpg.result: JPG files that open on the destination computer, with the originals still in HEIC.
heic-to-jpg.note: Open the convert tool in Safari or Chrome. Firefox on Windows often cannot decode HEIC. Convert a copy; keep the original if you still edit on iPhone.
heic-to-jpg.s1t: Know why the file is HEIC
heic-to-jpg.s1b: iPhone has saved HEIC by default since iOS 11. It is half the size of JPEG. Windows, WeChat, and many school forms still want JPG.
heic-to-jpg.s2t: Find the .HEIC in Files or Photos
heic-to-jpg.s2b: On Mac, export from Photos or copy from Files. AirDrop a HEIC to a PC and you will see .HEIC. Convert that copy, not a screenshot of the photo.
heic-to-jpg.s3t: Open convert in Safari or Chrome
heic-to-jpg.s3b: Firefox on Windows often cannot decode HEIC. If the preview is blank, switch browser — do not keep dropping the same file.
heic-to-jpg.s4b: Drop one or many .HEIC files. Choose JPG. Optional resize only if a form has a pixel cap.
heic-to-jpg.s5b: Download the JPG (or a ZIP of many). Keep the HEIC until you have opened the JPG.
heic-to-jpg.s6t: Open the JPG on the destination computer
heic-to-jpg.s6b: AirDrop or USB the JPG to Windows and double-click it. If Photos opens it, you are done. If it still fails, you sent the HEIC by mistake.
heic-to-jpg.s7t: Keep the original HEIC if you still edit on iPhone
heic-to-jpg.s7b: JPG is the copy you send. HEIC is the archive. Converting does not improve sharpness; it only changes compatibility.
heic-to-jpg.diagram1: Keep HEIC on the phone. Export JPG for Windows, WeChat, and forms.
heic-to-jpg.diagram2: Safari or Chrome, drop HEIC, pick JPG, download, open once.

jpg-to-pdf.name: How to convert JPG to PDF
jpg-to-pdf.blurb: Drop photos in order, pick A4 or fit-to-photo, download one PDF, flip every page.
jpg-to-pdf.title: How to convert JPG images to PDF
jpg-to-pdf.lead: You will make one PDF from several photos in this tab. List order is page order. Then you open the file and count.
jpg-to-pdf.result: A PDF with one page per photo, in the order you chose, that opens on a printer or a form upload.
jpg-to-pdf.note: Open the images-to-PDF tool when the photos are on disk. HEIC may fail in Firefox — convert to JPG first. Nothing is uploaded.
jpg-to-pdf.s1t: Put the photos in the order you want pages
jpg-to-pdf.s1b: Cover first, receipt last. Rename if it helps. One photo becomes one page.
jpg-to-pdf.s2t: Open JPG to PDF on cv.cm
jpg-to-pdf.s2b: Drop the files. Work stays in this tab.
jpg-to-pdf.s3t: Reorder if the list is wrong
jpg-to-pdf.s3b: The first row is page 1. Drag until the cover is on top.
jpg-to-pdf.s4b: A4 or Letter for printers and forms (photos get margins). Fit-to-photo fills the page — better for a lookbook, worse for office printers.
jpg-to-pdf.s5b: One file. Keep the photos until you have flipped the PDF.
jpg-to-pdf.s6b: Four photos should be four pages. If you see three, one file failed to decode — often HEIC in Firefox. Convert that one to JPG and add it.
jpg-to-pdf.diagram1: A4/Letter for forms. Fit-to-photo fills the page.
jpg-to-pdf.diagram2: Count pages after export. Do not trust the download toast alone.

pdf-to-jpg.name: How to convert PDF to JPG
pdf-to-jpg.blurb: Each page becomes an image. Choose 1× or 2×, download, open one file at 100%.
pdf-to-jpg.title: How to convert PDF to JPG
pdf-to-jpg.lead: You need images, not a PDF: a form, a slide, a chat that rejects PDF. Each page becomes a file. Check one at 100% before you send the ZIP.
pdf-to-jpg.result: One JPG (or PNG) per page, sharp enough to read, in a ZIP if there are many.
pdf-to-jpg.note: Open PDF-to-JPG on cv.cm when the PDF is on disk. Nothing is uploaded. Encrypted PDFs often cannot render until unlocked.
pdf-to-jpg.s1t: Confirm you need images, not a PDF
pdf-to-jpg.s1b: Chat apps, some forms, and slide tools want a picture. If they accept PDF, send the PDF — converting throws pixels into a bitmap.
pdf-to-jpg.s2t: Open PDF to JPG and drop the file
pdf-to-jpg.s2b: Work stays in this tab. If nothing appears, the PDF may be locked.
pdf-to-jpg.s3b: JPG for photos and chat. PNG if digits in a table must stay crisp. WebP is smaller but some forms reject it.
pdf-to-jpg.s4b: 1× for chat. 2× if you will zoom or reprint. Higher scale means a heavier ZIP.
pdf-to-jpg.s5t: Download a page or a ZIP
pdf-to-jpg.s5b: Many pages: ZIP is easier than saving one by one.
pdf-to-jpg.s6t: Open one file at 100% and read a line
pdf-to-jpg.s6b: If type smears, raise scale and use PNG. A thumbnail can look fine while the full page does not.
pdf-to-jpg.diagram1: 1× for chat. 2× if you will zoom or reprint.
pdf-to-jpg.diagram2: Open a page at 100% before you send the ZIP.

crop-photo.name: How to crop a photo
crop-photo.blurb: Pick 1:1, 4:5, or 16:9 first, move the box, check the four edges, reopen at 100%.
crop-photo.title: How to crop a photo (1:1, 4:5, iPhone)
crop-photo.lead: Cropping throws pixels away. Pick the ratio for the place you will post, move the subject, then reopen the export at 100%. Keep the original.
crop-photo.result: A crop that matches 1:1, 4:5, or 16:9, with intact heads and limbs, plus the original file still on disk.
crop-photo.note: Open the crop tool when the photo is on disk. HEIC may fail in Firefox — convert to JPG first. Nothing is uploaded.
crop-photo.s1t: Pick the ratio for the destination
crop-photo.s1b: 1:1 for avatars. 4:5 for a tall feed post (Instagram often shows this). 16:9 for a cover or landscape. 9:16 for stories. Pick the ratio before you move the box.
crop-photo.s2b: Drop the photo. Work stays in this tab.
crop-photo.s3t: Set the ratio, then move the subject
crop-photo.s3b: Do not freeform a feed post. Lock 4:5 (or 1:1), then drag. The subject can sit on a third line; that is optional, not a rule.
crop-photo.s4b: Leave space above the head. Do not cut skull, wrists, knees, or ankles. If they look left, leave space on the left. A half-object on the edge is clutter — pull it in or out.
crop-photo.s5b: Cropping cannot put pixels back. Keep the uncropped file beside the export.
crop-photo.s6b: The crop preview is small. Open the export full size. If an ear is gone, undo from the original — not from the crop.
crop-photo.diagram1: Same subject in 1:1, 4:5, and 16:9. Pick the ratio first.
crop-photo.diagram2: Leave headroom. Do not crop through joints. Reopen at 100%.

webp-to-png.name: How to convert WebP to PNG
webp-to-png.blurb: Chrome often saves WebP. Export PNG, then open it in the app that rejected WebP.
webp-to-png.title: How to convert WebP to PNG
webp-to-png.lead: Chrome and many sites save WebP. PNG opens in more apps and can keep a clear background. You will convert a copy in this tab and check the edges.
webp-to-png.result: PNG files that open in the app that rejected WebP, with transparency intact if the original had it.
webp-to-png.note: Open convert when the .webp is on disk. Pick PNG, not JPG, if you need a clear background. Nothing is uploaded.
webp-to-png.s1b: Some forms and older apps reject WebP. PNG keeps sharp edges and can keep transparency. JPG is smaller but fills a clear background.
webp-to-png.s2t: Open HEIC to JPG on cv.cm
webp-to-png.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
webp-to-png.s3b: One file or a batch. If the preview is blank, the browser cannot decode that WebP — try another browser.
webp-to-png.s4t: Choose PNG, not JPG, if you need transparency
webp-to-png.s4b: PNG keeps a clear background. JPG will fill it with white or a matte. Optional resize only if a form has a pixel cap.
webp-to-png.s5b: Keep the WebP until you have opened the PNG.
webp-to-png.s6t: Open it in the destination app
webp-to-png.s6b: If it still fails, you sent the WebP by mistake. If the background turned solid, you exported JPG.
webp-to-png.diagram1: WebP is smaller. PNG is accepted more widely and can keep a clear background.
webp-to-png.diagram2: Drop WebP, pick PNG, open the result. Do not pick JPG if you need transparency.

resize-image.name: How to resize or compress an image
resize-image.blurb: Set a real pixel cap or file-size cap, then open the download at 100%.
resize-image.title: How to resize or compress an image
resize-image.lead: Smaller pixels and a smaller file are different jobs. You will set a real size, pick JPEG quality if needed, then compare the download to the original.
resize-image.result: An image that meets a pixel cap or a file-size cap, still sharp enough to read.
resize-image.note: Open resize when the photo is on disk. Do not upscale a small photo and expect more detail. Nothing is uploaded.
resize-image.s1b: A form may want 1920 on the long edge. Email may want under 2 MB. An avatar may want 400×400. Pixels and kilobytes are not the same knob.
resize-image.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the photo.
resize-image.s3b: If the preview is blank, convert HEIC to JPG first, then come back.
resize-image.s4t: Set width and height with the lock on
resize-image.s4b: Or cap the long edge. Unlock only if you mean to stretch. Upscaling will not invent detail.
resize-image.s5t: If you need a smaller file, export JPEG and lower quality until it fits
resize-image.s5b: Watch the size estimate. PNG will not shrink much. Pick the largest file that still fits.
resize-image.s6b: If type smears, go back one quality step. A thumbnail can look fine while the full image does not.
resize-image.diagram1: Pixels vs kilobytes. A 4000px photo can still be a huge JPEG.
resize-image.diagram2: Keep the aspect lock. Then pick the largest file that still fits.

split-pdf.name: How to split a PDF
split-pdf.blurb: Every page as a file, or just pages 1–3. Download, then count.
split-pdf.title: How to split a PDF
split-pdf.lead: You need pages as separate files, or only a range. Split in this tab, then open the download and count.
split-pdf.result: One PDF per page in a ZIP, or one PDF with just the range you typed.
split-pdf.note: Open split PDF when the file is on disk. Locked PDFs often cannot split until unlocked. Nothing is uploaded.
split-pdf.s1t: Decide every page vs a range
split-pdf.s1b: Each page as its own PDF if you will send them around. A range like 1-3,5 if you only need those pages in one file.
split-pdf.s3t: Drop the PDF and note the page count
split-pdf.s3b: If nothing appears, the file may be locked. Unlock it first.
split-pdf.s4b: Ranges are inclusive. 1-3 is three pages. A comma starts another span.
split-pdf.s5b: Each-page mode packs a ZIP. A range is usually one PDF.
split-pdf.s6b: Ten pages split each-page should be ten files. A range 1-3 should be three pages in one PDF.
split-pdf.diagram1: Every page as its own PDF, packed in a ZIP.
split-pdf.diagram2: A range like 1-3,5 keeps those pages in one file.

add-watermark.name: How to add a watermark to a photo
add-watermark.blurb: Stamp a shop name or logo, set opacity, download, then check at 100%.
add-watermark.title: How to add a watermark to a photo
add-watermark.lead: A mark nobody can read is useless; a mark that hides the product is also useless. You will stamp text or a logo in this tab and check it at 100%.
add-watermark.result: Photos with a readable mark. The unmarked originals stay on disk.
add-watermark.note: This tool adds a mark. It will not remove someone else's watermark. Open it when the photos are on disk. Nothing is uploaded.
add-watermark.s1t: Decide text vs logo, corner vs tiled
add-watermark.s1b: Shop listings often tile a diagonal name. A single corner mark is quieter for a portrait. Do not copy another shop's mark.
add-watermark.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Batch is allowed.
add-watermark.s3t: Drop one photo or a batch
add-watermark.s3b: Keep the unmarked originals. You are making copies.
add-watermark.s4t: Type the name or drop a logo, then set opacity
add-watermark.s4b: High enough to read on a busy photo. Low enough to see the product. Tile if a corner mark is easy to crop off.
add-watermark.s5t: Download PNG, JPEG, or a ZIP
add-watermark.s5b: JPEG is smaller for shop listings. PNG if the mark has a clear background.
add-watermark.s6b: If the mark vanishes on a busy photo, raise contrast or tile it. If it hides the product, lower opacity.
add-watermark.diagram1: Corner mark vs tiled diagonal. Shop listings often tile.
add-watermark.diagram2: Opacity high enough to read, low enough to see the product.

remove-exif.name: How to remove EXIF / location from a photo
remove-exif.blurb: Phones store GPS in the file. Export a clean copy, then drop the export to prove it is gone.
remove-exif.title: How to remove EXIF / location from a photo
remove-exif.lead: Phones store GPS in the file. A listing or a chat can leak your address. You will export a clean copy in this tab and keep the original if you still need the map pin.
remove-exif.result: A photo that no longer carries GPS or camera EXIF, plus the original still on disk.
remove-exif.note: Open the EXIF tool when the photo is on disk. Re-encoding in this tab strips metadata. Screenshots often have none to begin with.
remove-exif.s1t: Check whether the file even has GPS
remove-exif.s1b: The tool shows if it is tagged. Screenshots and many chat exports already have none.
remove-exif.s2t: Open the EXIF tool on cv.cm
remove-exif.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
remove-exif.s3b: If it shows a location, that is the pin you are about to strip.
remove-exif.s4b: The canvas write does not copy EXIF. Keep the original if you still want the pin for yourself.
remove-exif.s5t: Drop the export back into the same tool
remove-exif.s5b: The second pass should show no location. If it still shows GPS, you opened the original by mistake.
remove-exif.s6t: Send the clean copy, keep the original if you need the pin
remove-exif.s6b: A chat app may strip GPS on its own. Do not trust that for a public listing — prove it with the second drop.
remove-exif.diagram1: Photo file = pixels + GPS. Export = pixels only.
remove-exif.diagram2: Drop, export, drop the export again. The second pass should be clean.

make-collage.name: How to make a photo collage
make-collage.blurb: Pick a grid, drop photos, choose contain vs cover, download, then check faces.
make-collage.title: How to make a photo collage
make-collage.lead: A collage is a layout first, then photos. You will pick a grid and a size, drop pictures in order, and check that faces were not cropped by Cover.
make-collage.result: One image with the photos in the right cells, faces intact, sized for the place you will post.
make-collage.note: Open collage when the photos are on disk. Contain keeps the whole photo (bars). Cover fills the cell and may crop. Nothing is uploaded.
make-collage.s1t: Pick the grid and the size first
make-collage.s1b: 2×2 or 3×3 for a set. Square for a feed, 4:5 portrait, 9:16 stories, 16:9 cover. Changing size later re-crops every cell.
make-collage.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
make-collage.s3t: Drop photos in the order they should appear
make-collage.s3b: First file is the first cell. Reorder before you export if the grid looks wrong.
make-collage.s4b: Contain keeps the whole photo and may add bars. Cover fills the cell and can cut a forehead or a chin. For faces, start with Contain.
make-collage.s5b: PNG for sharp edges. JPEG for a smaller feed upload.
make-collage.s6t: Open at 100% and walk the cells
make-collage.s6b: If a face is cut, switch that cell to Contain or pick a different photo. If the order is wrong, reorder and export again. Keep the originals.
make-collage.diagram2: Contain keeps the whole photo. Cover fills and may crop faces.

make-meme.name: How to make a meme
make-meme.blurb: Drop a photo, type top and bottom text, download a PNG, then check it at phone width.
make-meme.title: How to make a meme
make-meme.lead: A meme is a photo plus two short lines. You will drop an image, type top and bottom, and check that the type still reads at the size of a chat bubble.
make-meme.result: A PNG with readable top and bottom lines that do not cover the face.
make-meme.note: Open the meme tool when the photo is on disk. Keep lines short. Nothing is uploaded.
make-meme.s1t: Pick a photo that still reads small
make-meme.s1b: A busy background fights the type. A face or a clear object works better than a landscape.
make-meme.s3b: If the preview is blank, convert HEIC first.
make-meme.s4t: Type a short top and bottom line
make-meme.s4b: All caps is the usual look. Two to seven words per line. Do not write a paragraph.
make-meme.s5b: The outline is what keeps white type readable on a bright photo. If a line covers a face, shorten it.
make-meme.s6t: Download PNG and view at phone width
make-meme.s6b: If it only reads full-screen, it will fail in a chat. Keep the original unmarked photo.
make-meme.diagram1: Top line sets up. Bottom line pays off. Keep both short.
make-meme.diagram2: Stroke keeps type readable. Do not cover the face.

count-words.name: How to count words and characters
count-words.blurb: Paste the text, read the matching number, trim if a form has a cap.
count-words.title: How to count words and characters
count-words.lead: Essays want words. Forms often want characters. Chinese homework often wants characters with no spaces. You will paste the text and read the matching number.
count-words.result: The number the form or teacher actually asked for, from text that never left this tab.
count-words.note: Open word count when the text is ready. Words, characters, and characters without spaces are three different counts. Nothing is uploaded.
count-words.s1b: English essays: words. Twitter-style caps and many web forms: characters. Chinese homework: characters with spaces removed. Do not mix them.
count-words.s3t: Paste the text, or drop a .txt file
count-words.s3b: Paste from the same draft you will submit. Counting a different copy is how people miss the cap.
count-words.s4b: Words for English. Characters for most forms. Characters with no spaces for many CN assignments. CJK characters each count as a word here, so do not use Words for a 800-字 paper.
count-words.s5t: If there is a cap, trim and count again
count-words.s5b: Delete, then look at the same row. Do not switch from words to characters halfway.
count-words.s6t: Do not trust a different app's count for this form
count-words.s6b: Word, Google Docs, and a web form often disagree. Count in the same place you will paste.
count-words.diagram1: Words · characters · characters with no spaces. Three jobs, three numbers.
count-words.diagram2: For Chinese homework use characters with no spaces, not Words.

trim-audio.name: How to trim audio / cut an MP3
trim-audio.blurb: Set start and end, listen, download WAV, then play the file before you send it.
trim-audio.title: How to trim audio / cut an MP3
trim-audio.lead: You need a clip, not the whole file: a ring, a quote, a voicemail. You will mark start and end in this tab, listen, and download WAV. The original stays on disk.
trim-audio.result: A WAV that starts and ends where you marked, verified by playing it once.
trim-audio.note: Open trim when the audio is on disk. The download is WAV, even if you dropped an MP3. Listen before you send. Nothing is uploaded.
trim-audio.s1t: Know the start and end you want
trim-audio.s1b: A ringtone is often 20–40 seconds. A quote is one sentence. Write the times down if the file is long.
trim-audio.s3t: Drop the MP3, WAV, or M4A
trim-audio.s3b: If nothing plays, the codec may be unsupported. Try WAV or another browser.
trim-audio.s4t: Set start and end, then listen
trim-audio.s4b: Play the selection in the page. If the first word is clipped, nudge start earlier. If a breath hangs at the end, pull end in.
trim-audio.s5b: The export is WAV even if you started from MP3. If a form insists on MP3, convert the WAV afterwards. Keep the original.
trim-audio.s6b: Do not send on the in-page preview alone. If the start is late or the end is early, trim again.
trim-audio.diagram1: Start and end on the waveform. Listen to the selection before you download.
trim-audio.diagram2: Export is WAV. Play the file. The original MP3 stays on disk.

png-to-jpg.name: How to convert PNG to JPG
png-to-jpg.blurb: Pick JPG for a smaller photo. Check that a clear background became a solid matte, then compare file size.
png-to-jpg.title: How to convert PNG to JPG
png-to-jpg.lead: PNG is lossless and can keep a clear background. JPG is smaller and opens in more email and form uploads. You will convert a copy in this tab and check size plus the background.
png-to-jpg.result: A JPG that meets a size cap, with no leftover transparency, plus the original PNG still on disk.
png-to-jpg.note: Open convert when the .png is on disk. JPG has no alpha — a clear background becomes a solid matte, often black. Nothing is uploaded.
png-to-jpg.s1b: Email and many forms prefer JPG. Photos shrink. Logos, screenshots, and stickers with a clear background should stay PNG.
png-to-jpg.s2t: Open HEIC to JPG on cv.cm
png-to-jpg.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
png-to-jpg.s3b: One file or a batch. If the preview is blank, the browser cannot decode that PNG — try another file or browser.
png-to-jpg.s4b: Start near 0.9. A clear PNG background becomes a solid matte, often black. Optional max edge only if a form has a pixel cap.
png-to-jpg.s5b: Keep the PNG until you have opened the JPG and checked the size.
png-to-jpg.s6t: Open the JPG and compare size and background
png-to-jpg.s6b: If it is still huge, lower quality or cap the long edge. If a logo now sits on black, you needed PNG. If the form still rejects it, you sent the PNG by mistake.
png-to-jpg.diagram1: PNG keeps sharpness and transparency. JPG is smaller and has no alpha.
png-to-jpg.diagram2: A clear PNG background becomes a solid matte in JPG, often black.

jpg-to-png.name: How to convert JPG to PNG
jpg-to-png.blurb: Pick PNG for lossless edits or a form that wants PNG. It will not punch a hole in the background. The file usually gets larger.
jpg-to-png.title: How to convert JPG to PNG
jpg-to-png.lead: JPG is already lossy. PNG will not restore detail and will not invent transparency. You convert when a tool or form wants PNG, or before you crop the same photo many times.
jpg-to-png.result: A PNG that the destination accepts, still opaque, usually larger than the JPG, with the original still on disk.
jpg-to-png.note: Open convert when the .jpg is on disk. PNG does not remove a photo background. Nothing is uploaded.
jpg-to-png.s1b: A form or an editor may insist on PNG. Do not convert to 'add transparency' — a JPG has no alpha to keep.
jpg-to-png.s2t: Open HEIC to JPG on cv.cm
jpg-to-png.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
jpg-to-png.s3b: One file or a batch. If the preview is blank, try another browser.
jpg-to-png.s4t: Pick PNG. Do not expect a clear background
jpg-to-png.s4b: The pixels stay opaque. Quality has no slider on PNG. Optional max edge only if a form has a pixel cap.
jpg-to-png.s5b: Keep the JPG until you have opened the PNG.
jpg-to-png.s6t: Open it and expect a larger file
jpg-to-png.s6b: If you needed a sticker with a hole, this conversion cannot do that. If the form still wants JPG, send the original.
jpg-to-png.diagram1: JPG is already lossy. PNG will not restore detail.
jpg-to-png.diagram2: Converting JPG to PNG does not make the background transparent.

avif-to-jpg.name: How to convert AVIF to JPG
avif-to-jpg.blurb: Chrome often saves AVIF. Export JPG, then open it on the PC or form that rejected AVIF.
avif-to-jpg.title: How to convert AVIF to JPG
avif-to-jpg.lead: AVIF is smaller. JPG opens on older Windows, print shops, and many chat apps. You will convert a copy in this tab and open the JPG once before sending.
avif-to-jpg.result: JPG files that open where AVIF was rejected, with the original AVIF still on disk.
avif-to-jpg.note: Open convert in a current Chrome, Edge, or Safari. Older browsers may not decode AVIF. Convert a copy. Nothing is uploaded.
avif-to-jpg.s1t: Know why the file is AVIF
avif-to-jpg.s1b: Chrome and many sites save AVIF because it is smaller than JPG. Windows Photos, WeChat, and print kiosks often still want JPG.
avif-to-jpg.s2t: Open convert in a current browser
avif-to-jpg.s2b: Chrome, Edge, or recent Safari. If the preview is blank, switch browser — do not keep dropping the same file.
avif-to-jpg.s3b: One file or a batch. Convert a copy; keep the AVIF if you still archive it.
avif-to-jpg.s4b: Start near 0.9 quality. Optional max edge only if a form has a pixel cap. Pick PNG only if you need a lossless copy, not for chat.
avif-to-jpg.s5b: Keep the AVIF until you have opened the JPG.
avif-to-jpg.s6t: Open the JPG where AVIF failed
avif-to-jpg.s6b: If it still fails, you sent the AVIF by mistake. Converting does not add sharpness.
avif-to-jpg.diagram1: AVIF is smaller. JPG opens on older Windows, print, and chat.
avif-to-jpg.diagram2: Drop AVIF, pick JPG, open the result on the destination that rejected AVIF.

rotate-photo.name: How to rotate or flip a photo
rotate-photo.blurb: Turn 90° or 180°, or flip a mirror. Download, then open the file — not only the preview.
rotate-photo.title: How to rotate or flip a photo
rotate-photo.lead: Rotate turns the photo. Flip is a mirror. You will pick one, export a copy, and open that file so Windows or a form sees the pixels, not leftover EXIF.
rotate-photo.result: A download that is upright (or mirrored on purpose), verified by opening the file, with the original still on disk.
rotate-photo.note: Open rotate when the photo is on disk. 90° chips for phone shots; flip for a mirror selfie. Export writes pixels, so a sideways EXIF photo can become actually upright. Nothing is uploaded.
rotate-photo.s1b: A sideways phone photo needs 90° left or right. Upside down needs 180°. Text that reads backward needs a horizontal flip, not a rotation.
rotate-photo.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the photo.
rotate-photo.s3b: If the preview is blank, convert HEIC or AVIF to JPG first, then come back. The preview already applies EXIF orientation.
rotate-photo.s4b: Phone shots: 90° left, 90° right, or 180°. The angle slider is for a small tilt. Flip horizontal for a mirror selfie. Flip vertical only if the photo is truly upside-down in a mirror sense.
rotate-photo.s5b: PNG if you need sharp type or a clear background. JPG for a smaller send. Keep the original until you have opened the download.
rotate-photo.s6b: Do not trust the in-page preview alone. If Explorer still shows it sideways, you sent the original. If letters are backward, you flipped when you needed 90°.
rotate-photo.diagram1: Rotate 90° / 180° turns the photo. Flip is a mirror.
rotate-photo.diagram2: Export writes pixels. Open the file so EXIF-only sideways photos become actually upright.

png-to-webp.name: How to convert PNG to WebP
png-to-webp.blurb: Pick WebP for a smaller file that can keep a clear background. Then open it in a browser, not in an old form.
png-to-webp.title: How to convert PNG to WebP
png-to-webp.lead: WebP is smaller than PNG and can keep transparency, unlike JPG. You convert a copy for the web, then check the file in a current browser.
png-to-webp.result: A WebP that is smaller than the PNG, with transparency intact if the original had it, plus the PNG still on disk.
png-to-webp.note: Open convert when the .png is on disk. Pick WebP, not JPG, if you need a clear background. Old forms may still reject WebP. Nothing is uploaded.
png-to-webp.s1b: A site or a chat that accepts WebP will load faster. Email and many school forms still want PNG or JPG. Do not convert if the destination rejects WebP.
png-to-webp.s2t: Open HEIC to JPG on cv.cm
png-to-webp.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
png-to-webp.s3b: One file or a batch. If the preview is blank, try another browser.
png-to-webp.s4t: Pick WebP, not JPG, if you need transparency
png-to-webp.s4b: WebP can keep a clear background. JPG will fill it. Start quality near 0.9. Optional max edge only if a page has a pixel cap.
png-to-webp.s5b: Keep the PNG until you have opened the WebP.
png-to-webp.s6t: Open it in a current browser
png-to-webp.s6b: Check the edges and the file size against the PNG. If a form still rejects it, send the PNG. Converting does not add sharpness.
png-to-webp.diagram1: WebP is smaller than PNG and can keep a clear background. JPG cannot.
png-to-webp.diagram2: Pick WebP to keep alpha. Open it in a browser. Old forms may still want PNG.

mp3-to-wav.name: How to convert MP3 to WAV
mp3-to-wav.blurb: Drop the MP3, pick a sample rate if you need one, download WAV, then play the file. The original stays on disk.
mp3-to-wav.title: How to convert MP3 to WAV
mp3-to-wav.lead: A DAW, an editor, or a form may want WAV, not MP3. You will decode a copy in this tab, pick 44.1 or 48 kHz if you need a target, and play the download.
mp3-to-wav.result: A WAV that plays, at the sample rate you chose, with the original MP3 still on disk.
mp3-to-wav.note: Open MP3 to WAV when the audio is on disk. The download is WAV even if you dropped M4A. Listen before you send. Nothing is uploaded.
mp3-to-wav.s1b: WAV is uncompressed PCM. Editors and some upload forms want it. It will be much larger than the MP3. Do not convert just to 'improve quality' — you cannot get back what MP3 already threw away.
mp3-to-wav.s2t: Open MP3 to WAV on cv.cm
mp3-to-wav.s3t: Drop the MP3, M4A, or WAV
mp3-to-wav.s3b: If nothing plays, this browser cannot decode that codec. Try WAV or another browser. Safari and Chrome usually handle MP3.
mp3-to-wav.s4b: Leave original if you are unsure. 44.1 is the CD / music default. 48 is the video default. Resampling does not add highs.
mp3-to-wav.s5b: Keep the MP3 until you have played the WAV.
mp3-to-wav.s6b: Do not send on the in-page player alone. If it is silent, the codec failed. If a form still wants MP3, send the original.
mp3-to-wav.diagram1: WAV is uncompressed. MP3 already threw data away. Converting does not restore it.
mp3-to-wav.diagram2: 44.1 kHz for music. 48 kHz for video. Play the downloaded WAV.

join-audio.name: How to join audio files / merge MP3s
join-audio.blurb: Drop two or more clips in order, download one WAV, then play the file from start to end.
join-audio.title: How to join audio files / merge MP3s
join-audio.lead: You need one file, not a playlist: intro then song, two voice notes, a bed under a voicemail. List order is playback order. Export is WAV.
join-audio.result: One WAV that plays the clips in the order you set, verified from start to end, with the originals still on disk.
join-audio.note: Open join when the clips are on disk. You need two or more. Later clips are resampled to the first clip's rate. Download is WAV. Nothing is uploaded.
join-audio.s1t: Put the clips in playback order
join-audio.s1b: Intro first, bed last. Rename if it helps. You will still be able to move rows after you drop them.
join-audio.s3b: One file is not a join. If a row shows an error, that codec failed — convert that clip to WAV first, or skip it.
join-audio.s4t: Reorder if the list is wrong
join-audio.s4b: The first row plays first. Later clips are resampled to the first clip's sample rate so the join does not drift.
join-audio.s5b: Export is WAV even if every source was MP3. Keep the originals until you have listened through.
join-audio.s6t: Play the file from start to end
join-audio.s6b: Listen for a missing clip, a gap, or a pitch change at a join. If the order is wrong, move rows and export again. Do not send on the in-page list alone.
join-audio.diagram1: List order is playback order. You need two or more clips.
join-audio.diagram2: Export is one WAV. Later clips match the first clip's sample rate.

make-favicon.name: How to make a favicon
make-favicon.blurb: Crop to a square, pick Cover or Contain, download ICO plus PNG sizes, then check the 16-pixel version.
make-favicon.title: How to make a favicon
make-favicon.lead: A favicon has to read at 16 pixels. You will square the mark, choose Cover or Contain, and download an ICO for classic tabs plus a PNG zip for touch icons.
make-favicon.result: A favicon.ico (16/32/48) and a PNG zip (including 180/192/512) that still reads at tab size.
make-favicon.note: Open favicon when the mark is on disk. Cover fills the square and may crop. Contain letterboxes. White background is on by default. Nothing is uploaded.
make-favicon.s1t: Start from a mark that still reads tiny
make-favicon.s1b: A busy photo dies at 16 pixels. A letter, a simple shape, or a high-contrast logo works. Crop the subject before you come here if the frame is wide.
make-favicon.s3b: If the preview is blank, convert HEIC first.
make-favicon.s4t: Choose Cover or Contain, and white background
make-favicon.s4b: Cover fills the square and may crop. Contain keeps the whole mark and letterboxes. Leave white background on for a classic tab. Uncheck it if you need a transparent PNG.
make-favicon.s5t: Download ICO and the PNG zip
make-favicon.s5b: ICO packs 16, 32, and 48 for classic tabs. The zip also has 180, 192, and 512 for Apple touch and PWA icons. Keep the original mark.
make-favicon.s6b: The 256 preview lies. If the 16px file is a blur, simplify the mark or switch to Contain. Put favicon.ico at the site root and link the PNGs in the HTML.
make-favicon.diagram1: Cover fills and may crop. Contain keeps the whole mark and letterboxes.
make-favicon.diagram2: ICO is 16/32/48. PNG zip adds 180/192/512. Check the 16px file.

make-signature.name: How to draw a signature PNG
make-signature.blurb: Draw on the pad, download a cropped PNG, then check it at the size of the form. Not a legal e-sign.
make-signature.title: How to draw a signature PNG
make-signature.lead: You need a picture of your name, not a legally binding e-sign. You will draw in this tab, download a PNG cropped to the ink, and check it at the size of the box on the form.
make-signature.result: A PNG cropped to the ink, readable at form size, that is not a legal e-sign.
make-signature.note: Open signature when you are ready to draw. The preview pad is cream; the PNG is cropped to the ink with a clear background. Not a legal e-sign and not a stamp on a PDF. Nothing is uploaded.
make-signature.s1t: Know this is a picture, not a legal e-sign
make-signature.s1b: Banks and governments want a qualified e-sign or a wet signature. This PNG is for a form that asks you to paste an image of your name. It does not bind a PDF.
make-signature.s3t: Draw with a finger, a stylus, or a mouse
make-signature.s3b: One continuous name is easier to crop than scattered initials. Undo the last stroke if a loop went wrong. A mouse is worse than a finger.
make-signature.s4b: Export crops to the ink and drops the cream pad. The background is clear. If the download is empty, you had no strokes.
make-signature.s5t: Open it at the size of the form box
make-signature.s5b: A signature that only reads full-screen will smear in a 200-pixel box. If it is too thin, draw again thicker. Keep the PNG; do not photograph the pad.
make-signature.s6t: Do not treat this as a signed PDF
make-signature.s6b: If the destination wants a signature on a PDF page, that is a different job. Paste the PNG only where the form asks for an image.
make-signature.diagram1: This is a picture of a name. It is not a legal e-sign and it does not bind a PDF.
make-signature.diagram2: Export crops to the ink. The PNG background is clear. Check it at form size.

annotate-screenshot.name: How to annotate a screenshot
annotate-screenshot.blurb: Drop a screenshot, add a box, an arrow, or a label, download a PNG, then check it at the size you will send.
annotate-screenshot.title: How to annotate a screenshot
annotate-screenshot.lead: A bug report, a how-to, or a chat needs a mark on the picture, not a paragraph. You will drop a screenshot, draw a box or an arrow, and check the PNG at the size of a message.
annotate-screenshot.result: A PNG with a box, an arrow, or a short label that still reads at chat size, plus the original unmarked file.
annotate-screenshot.note: Open screenshot when the capture is on disk or on the clipboard. Rect, arrow, or text. Export is PNG. The original stays. Nothing is uploaded.
annotate-screenshot.s1t: Decide box, arrow, or a short label
annotate-screenshot.s1b: A box around the broken control. An arrow at the button to tap. Two or three words, not a paragraph. Too many marks fight the screenshot.
annotate-screenshot.s3b: Paste from the clipboard if you just captured. If the preview is blank, the file is not an image this browser can decode.
annotate-screenshot.s4b: Rect around the area. Arrow at the tap. Text for a two-word label. Undo the last mark if it covers the thing you meant to show.
annotate-screenshot.s5b: Keep the unmarked original. Export does not change the file on disk.
annotate-screenshot.s6t: Open it at chat or ticket size
annotate-screenshot.s6b: If the arrow vanishes when small, draw it thicker and closer. If type smears, shorten the label. Do not send the unmarked original by mistake.
annotate-screenshot.diagram1: Box the broken control. Arrow the tap. Two words, not a paragraph.
annotate-screenshot.diagram2: Export is PNG. Keep the unmarked original. Check at chat size.

make-invoice.name: How to make an invoice PDF
make-invoice.blurb: Fill from/to, add line items, check tax and total, download a PDF, then read the numbers once. Not a tax form.
make-invoice.title: How to make an invoice PDF
make-invoice.lead: A simple bill: who you are, who pays, what was sold, tax, due date. You will fill the fields in this tab, check the totals, and open the PDF. This is not a government tax form.
make-invoice.result: A one-page PDF whose line amounts and tax match the fields you typed, opened once before you send it.
make-invoice.note: Open invoice when you know the parties and the lines. Tax is a percent on the subtotal. Not a VAT return and not a legal e-invoice. Nothing is uploaded.
make-invoice.s1t: Gather from, bill-to, and the lines
make-invoice.s1b: A name and address on each side. One row per thing sold: description, quantity, unit price. Write the currency and the tax percent the contract uses.
make-invoice.s3t: Fill the parties, number, dates, and currency
make-invoice.s3b: Due should be on or after the invoice date. Pick the currency the buyer will actually pay.
make-invoice.s4t: Add each line: description, qty, price
make-invoice.s4b: Amount is qty × price. Empty descriptions make a messy PDF. Add a line per item, not a paragraph in one row.
make-invoice.s5t: Set tax percent and read the totals
make-invoice.s5b: Tax is a percent of the subtotal. 0 if the sale is untaxed here. The preview total must match qty × price plus tax before you download.
make-invoice.s6t: Download the PDF and open it
make-invoice.s6b: One page. Read from, bill-to, each line, tax, and total. If a number is wrong, fix the field and export again. This file is not a VAT filing.
make-invoice.diagram1: From, bill-to, and one line per item. Amount is qty × price.
make-invoice.diagram2: Tax is a percent of the subtotal. Open the PDF. This is not a tax return.

make-password.name: How to generate a strong password
make-password.blurb: Set length and character types, copy once, paste into the account, then close the tab. Do not email it.
make-password.title: How to generate a strong password
make-password.lead: A unique password for one account. You will set length and character types in this tab, copy once, and paste into the signup. Random bytes come from this device. Do not reuse it.
make-password.result: A random password you pasted into one account, that never left this tab except via copy, and that you will not email.
make-password.note: Open password when you are creating or resetting one account. Default length 16. Exclude similar drops 0 O I l 1. Nothing is uploaded.
make-password.s1t: Use a unique password for this account
make-password.s1b: Reusing a password is how one leak opens the rest. A password manager can store it. Do not recycle a phrase you already typed on another site.
make-password.s2b: Generation stays in this tab. Random bytes come from Web Crypto on this device.
make-password.s3b: Default is 16. Longer is stronger if the site allows it. Below 12 is for the sites that still cap length, not a goal.
make-password.s4t: Keep letters, digits, and symbols unless the site forbids them
make-password.s4b: Exclude similar drops 0, O, I, l, and 1 so you can read it. If a bank form rejects symbols, turn symbols off for that account only.
make-password.s5t: Copy once and paste into the account
make-password.s5b: Do not screenshot it. Do not put it in email or chat. A password manager is the place to store it after paste.
make-password.s6b: Closing discards the password from this page. If you did not store it, generate a new one — do not try to remember a random string.
make-password.diagram1: Length 16+. Letters, digits, symbols. Exclude 0 O I l 1 if you will type it.
make-password.diagram2: Copy once. Paste into one account. Do not email it. Close the tab.

format-json.name: How to format JSON
format-json.blurb: Pretty-print with two spaces or minify to one line, then copy the output. Comments and trailing commas are not JSON.
format-json.title: How to format JSON
format-json.lead: You have text that should be JSON. You will paste it in this tab, pick pretty or minify, and copy a result that parsed. A log prefix in front of the brace is not JSON yet.
format-json.result: JSON that parsed: two-space indent, or one line, with the same keys and values you pasted.
format-json.note: Open the JSON formatter when the text is in front of you. Pretty uses two spaces. Minify is one line. Nothing is uploaded.
format-json.s1t: Decide reading layout or one line
format-json.s1b: Pretty is for reading. Minify is for a header, a query, or a small file. Both parse first. Invalid text is not repaired for you.
format-json.s2t: Open the JSON formatter on cv.cm
format-json.s3t: Paste the value, not the log prefix
format-json.s3b: Start at the first { or [ and stop at its match. A time or the word INFO in front makes the whole paste invalid.
format-json.s4t: If it says invalid, fix the text
format-json.s4b: JSON wants double quotes, no comments, and no comma after the last item. Single quotes, undefined, and NaN are not JSON. An integer longer than 15 digits must be a string in quotes, or the digits can change.
format-json.s5b: Pretty is a two-space indent. Minify is one line. Copy that box, not the broken input.
format-json.s6t: Check one value you already know
format-json.s6b: A name, a count, or an id. If a long number changed, it was a bare integer past the safe range. Put it in quotes and format again.
format-json.diagram1: Pretty is two spaces for reading. Minify is one line for sending. Both must parse.
format-json.diagram2: Copy the output. An integer longer than 15 digits belongs in quotes.

decode-base64.name: How to decode Base64
decode-base64.blurb: Decode standard Base64 to UTF-8 text, or encode text the other way. Minus and underscore are refused. A picture is not text.
decode-base64.title: How to decode Base64
decode-base64.lead: You have a Base64 string, or text to encode. You will pick decode or encode in this tab and copy real text. This page prints UTF-8. It does not rebuild a PNG or a PDF.
decode-base64.result: UTF-8 text from standard Base64, or standard Base64 from the text you typed.
decode-base64.note: Open Base64 when the string is in front of you. Decode wants A–Z, a–z, 0–9, plus, slash, and = padding. Nothing is uploaded.
decode-base64.s1t: Look at the alphabet before you paste
decode-base64.s1b: Standard Base64 uses plus and slash. URL-safe uses minus and underscore. This page accepts only the standard alphabet. A data: prefix is not part of the payload.
decode-base64.s3b: Decode turns Base64 into text. Encode turns text into Base64 using UTF-8 bytes. Encoding a string that is already Base64 wraps it a second time.
decode-base64.s4b: Line breaks and spaces are removed on decode. After that, the length must be a multiple of 4, with = only at the end.
decode-base64.s5t: If decode fails, it is not UTF-8 text
decode-base64.s5b: Minus and underscore are refused. Missing = fails. A PNG, a PDF, or a data URL is bytes, so this page will not print it. Swap minus to plus and underscore to slash, and pad with =, only when you know the payload is text.
decode-base64.s6t: Copy and check a word you expect
decode-base64.s6b: If the text is garbled, the bytes were not UTF-8. Drop that result. To check an encode, decode the output and you should see the same text.
decode-base64.diagram1: Standard uses plus and slash. URL-safe uses minus and underscore. This page wants standard Base64.
decode-base64.diagram2: Decode prints UTF-8 text. A picture or a PDF fails. Copy a word you recognize.

unix-time.name: How to convert a Unix timestamp
unix-time.blurb: Count the digits, paste seconds or milliseconds, then read ISO and local time. Do not convert the number twice.
unix-time.title: How to convert a Unix timestamp
unix-time.lead: A log, an API, or a database gave you a number. You will count digits, paste it in this tab, and read UTC and local time. Ten digits are seconds. Thirteen are milliseconds.
unix-time.result: Seconds, milliseconds, an ISO time in UTC, and local wall time for one instant, with a year you already expected.
unix-time.note: Open the timestamp tool when you have the number or an ISO date. Now fills the current second. Nothing is uploaded.
unix-time.s1b: Ten digits are seconds. Thirteen are milliseconds. Sixteen are microseconds, and this page divides those by 1,000 once. If you already multiplied by 1,000, leave the original number alone.
unix-time.s2t: Open the timestamp tool on cv.cm
unix-time.s3t: Paste the number, an ISO date, or tap Now
unix-time.s3b: 1700000000 is seconds. 1700000000000 is milliseconds. 2023-11-14T22:13:20Z is a date. Now writes the current Unix second.
unix-time.s4t: Read seconds, milliseconds, ISO, UTC, and local
unix-time.s4b: ISO and the UTC line are the same instant in UTC. Local is that instant on this computer. Copy puts all of them on the clipboard.
unix-time.s5t: A wild year means the digits were wrong
unix-time.s5b: A year like 50000 means milliseconds were read as seconds, or you converted twice. A year in 1970 means the number was divided too far. Paste the original number again.
unix-time.s6t: Copy the line the other system asked for
unix-time.s6b: An API that wants seconds does not want the ISO string. A spreadsheet that wants a date does not want thirteen digits. Match the field.
unix-time.diagram1: 10 digits: seconds. 13 digits: milliseconds. 16 digits: microseconds, divided by 1,000 once.
unix-time.diagram2: Read ISO and local time. A wild year means the digits were wrong.

read-jwt.name: How to read a JWT
read-jwt.blurb: Paste a token, read the header and payload, and look at exp. The signature stays unchecked. A decoded token is only JSON you can see.
read-jwt.title: How to read a JWT
read-jwt.lead: You need to see the claims. You will paste the token in this tab, read alg and the payload, and close the tab. Decoding shows JSON. It leaves the signature unchecked.
read-jwt.result: A header and a payload you can read, plus an expiry line that only compares exp with the clock.
read-jwt.note: Open the JWT decoder when the token is on the clipboard. Three parts separated by dots is the usual shape. The signature stays unchecked. Nothing is uploaded.
read-jwt.s1t: Reading shows JSON. The signature stays unchecked
read-jwt.s1b: Anyone can change the payload and encode it again. This page shows the JSON. It does not check the signature, the issuer, or the audience. A tidy payload is a reason to read it, and a reason to verify it somewhere that holds the key.
read-jwt.s2t: Open the JWT decoder on cv.cm
read-jwt.s3b: The usual shape is three parts separated by dots. Two parts can still decode. A live access token can hold an email or a user id. Keep it off chat, and keep this tab off a shared screen.
read-jwt.s4b: alg is a label, including the word none. It is a label only. Look for iss, aud, sub, and exp. If the page cannot decode it, the header or the payload is not base64url JSON.
read-jwt.s5t: Expired compares exp with the clock
read-jwt.s5b: exp is seconds. If that instant is in the past, the line says expired. Missing exp means there is no expiry claim to compare. In both cases the signature stayed unchecked.
read-jwt.s6b: Closing discards the token from this page. When you need a trusted token, verify it where the secret or the public key lives. This page has neither.
read-jwt.diagram1: Decode shows JSON. The signature stays unchecked. Verify where the key lives.
read-jwt.diagram2: Expired compares exp with the clock. The signature stayed unchecked.

count-workdays.name: How to count business days
count-workdays.blurb: Count Monday through Friday between two dates, including both ends. A Wednesday holiday stays in the count.
count-workdays.title: How to count business days
count-workdays.lead: You need the weekdays in a span. You will pick two dates in this tab and read the business-day number. Saturdays and Sundays are the only days left out. A public holiday on Wednesday still counts.
count-workdays.result: A business-day number that includes both dates when they are weekdays, plus the weekend days in that same span.
count-workdays.note: Open business days when you know the two calendar dates. The span includes both ends. Nothing is uploaded.
count-workdays.s1b: Monday 5 January 2026 through Friday 9 January 2026 is five business days. Friday through the next Monday is two, because Saturday and Sunday sit in the middle.
count-workdays.s2b: The count stays in this tab.
count-workdays.s3t: Pick the start and the end
count-workdays.s3b: Use the calendar dates on the form. If the end is before the start, the business-day number is negative. The weekend count stays zero or positive.
count-workdays.s4t: Read business days and weekend days
count-workdays.s4b: Business days are Monday through Friday. Weekend days are the Saturdays and Sundays inside the same inclusive span.
count-workdays.s5b: A holiday on Wednesday is still a business day here. If the form skips holidays, subtract those dates after you copy the number.
count-workdays.s6b: A same-day weekday is 1. A same-day Saturday or Sunday is 0. This page includes both ends. A plain day difference of the same dates is one smaller when the span is positive.
count-workdays.diagram1: Both ends count. Monday 5 Jan through Friday 9 Jan 2026 is 5 business days.
count-workdays.diagram2: Weekends drop out. A Wednesday holiday stays in the count.

simplify-fraction.name: How to simplify a fraction
simplify-fraction.blurb: Reduce a whole numerator and denominator, or turn a decimal into a fraction. 4/6 becomes 2/3. A decimal stops at denominator 10,000.
simplify-fraction.title: How to simplify a fraction
simplify-fraction.lead: You have 4/6 or 0.75 and you need the short fraction. You will simplify in this tab and copy the fraction text. 5/2 stays 5/2. This page does not print a mixed number such as 2 1/2.
simplify-fraction.result: A reduced fraction such as 2/3 or 3/4, with the sign on the numerator, and a decimal line you can check.
simplify-fraction.note: Open the fraction calculator when you have the two whole numbers or the decimal. Denominator 0 fails. Nothing is uploaded.
simplify-fraction.s1t: Decide simplify or from a decimal
simplify-fraction.s1b: Whole numbers use simplify. 4 and 6 become 2/3. A decimal such as 0.75 uses the other mode and becomes 3/4. The sign stays on the numerator. A negative denominator flips.
simplify-fraction.s2t: Open the fraction calculator on cv.cm
simplify-fraction.s2b: The math stays in this tab.
simplify-fraction.s3t: Enter whole numbers, or one decimal
simplify-fraction.s3b: Denominator 0 fails. A decimal typed into the numerator is rejected in simplify mode. Switch mode instead of rounding it yourself first.
simplify-fraction.s4t: Read the fraction and the decimal line
simplify-fraction.s4b: Copy keeps the fraction text, such as 2/3. The decimal line is the check. If it does not match the number you meant, the input was only approximated.
simplify-fraction.s5t: A long decimal stops at denominator 10,000
simplify-fraction.s5b: 0.333333 becomes 1/3. A decimal that is not a short fraction stays close once the denominator would pass 10,000. Read the decimal line again.
simplify-fraction.s6t: Keep it as an improper fraction
simplify-fraction.s6b: 5/2 stays 5/2. If a worksheet wants 2 1/2, split the whole part after you copy.
simplify-fraction.diagram1: 4/6 becomes 2/3. The sign stays on the numerator.
simplify-fraction.diagram2: 0.75 becomes 3/4. A long decimal stops at denominator 10,000.

hourly-pay.name: How to convert hourly pay to a yearly salary
hourly-pay.blurb: Multiply one hourly rate by hours per week and weeks per year. The default is 40 by 52, which is 2,080 hours. The result is gross pay.
hourly-pay.title: How to convert hourly pay to a yearly salary
hourly-pay.lead: You want the yearly gross from an hourly rate, or the hourly rate from a yearly gross. You will set hours and weeks in this tab. Tax, insurance, and a higher overtime rate stay outside this number.
hourly-pay.result: Hourly, weekly, and yearly gross pay from one rate, one hours-per-week, and one weeks-per-year.
hourly-pay.note: Open hourly to yearly when you know the rate. Defaults are 40 hours and 52 weeks. Gross pay only. Nothing is uploaded.
hourly-pay.s1t: Use one rate and the real weeks
hourly-pay.s1b: 20 an hour, 40 hours a week, 52 weeks, is 41,600.00 gross. Two unpaid weeks make it 50 weeks, not 52. Overtime at time-and-a-half is a second rate. This page uses one.
hourly-pay.s2t: Open hourly to yearly on cv.cm
hourly-pay.s2b: The math stays in this tab.
hourly-pay.s3b: Hourly to yearly multiplies. Yearly to hourly divides the yearly gross by hours times weeks. A blank field fails.
hourly-pay.s4b: Hours must be greater than 0 and at most 168. Weeks must be greater than 0 and at most 52. 40 and 52 are the defaults: 2,080 hours.
hourly-pay.s5b: All three are gross, shown to two decimals. Weekly is the hourly rate times hours per week. Yearly is weekly times weeks.
hourly-pay.s6b: Copy the three lines. Subtract tax, insurance, or pension on the form that asks for net pay. This gross figure is not take-home.
hourly-pay.diagram1: 20 × 40 hours × 52 weeks = 41,600.00 gross. Unpaid weeks lower the 52.
hourly-pay.diagram2: One rate. Gross only. Tax and overtime premiums stay outside.

convert-timezone.name: How to convert a time zone
convert-timezone.blurb: Pick the zone that owns the clock you were given, then the other zone. Daylight saving follows the date. Copy is the UTC instant.
convert-timezone.title: How to convert a time zone
convert-timezone.lead: Someone named a clock time in one city. You will choose that zone as the source and the other zone as the destination, then read the offset. Adding the offset again after the page has converted the time moves the meeting.
convert-timezone.result: The same instant on the other zone's clock, with the offset for that date, and a UTC instant you can copy.
convert-timezone.note: Open the timezone converter when you know which zone owns the clock. Now fills the current wall time in the source zone. Nothing is uploaded.
convert-timezone.s1t: Name the zone that owns the clock
convert-timezone.s1b: A 9:00 from a New York calendar belongs to America/New_York, even if you are in Shanghai. The source is their clock. The destination is the clock you need.
convert-timezone.s2t: Open the timezone converter on cv.cm
convert-timezone.s3t: Set both zones and the date-time
convert-timezone.s3b: Now fills the current wall time in the source zone. The date matters because the offset can change.
convert-timezone.s4t: Read the offset on that date
convert-timezone.s4b: New York in January is UTC−05:00. In July it is UTC−04:00. The page uses the IANA rule for the date you picked. A skipped hour in spring does not exist. A repeated hour in autumn happens twice. If your time sits in that gap or overlap, read the offset before you trust the wall time.
convert-timezone.s5b: Copy puts the ISO time in UTC on the clipboard. That is the same moment. It is the instant, and the wall-clock line stays on the page. An API that wants UTC wants that ISO string.
convert-timezone.s6t: Leave the offset where the page put it
convert-timezone.s6b: The result is already the other zone's clock. Adding +8 or −5 again moves the meeting. Compare one known moment, such as 12:00 in the source zone, before you send the time.
convert-timezone.diagram1: Source is the zone that owns the clock. Destination is the clock you need.
convert-timezone.diagram2: January in New York is UTC−05:00. July is UTC−04:00. Copy the UTC instant.

profit-margin.name: How to calculate a profit margin
profit-margin.blurb: Divide profit by the selling price for margin, and by the cost for markup. Cost 50 and price 80 is a 37.50% margin and a 60.00% markup.
profit-margin.title: How to calculate a profit margin
profit-margin.lead: You have a cost and a selling price. You will read profit, margin, and markup in this tab. Margin divides by the price. Markup divides by the cost. They are not the same percent.
profit-margin.result: Profit, a margin percent of the selling price, and a markup percent of the cost, for amounts that are zero or more.
profit-margin.note: Open profit margin when you know both amounts. A zero price has no margin percent. A zero cost has no markup percent. Nothing is uploaded.
profit-margin.s1b: Cost is what you paid. Price is what the buyer pays. Profit is price minus cost. A 30% margin is not a 30% markup.
profit-margin.s2b: The math stays in this tab.
profit-margin.s3b: Both amounts must be zero or more. Both zero fails. Cost 50 and price 80 is the check: profit 30.00.
profit-margin.s4t: Read margin and markup as different percents
profit-margin.s4b: Margin is profit divided by the price: 30 / 80 is 37.50%. Markup is profit divided by the cost: 30 / 50 is 60.00%. Copy the line the form asked for.
profit-margin.s5t: A zero price or a zero cost drops one percent
profit-margin.s5b: A zero price has profit and markup, and the margin line is a dash. A zero cost has profit and margin, and the markup line is a dash.
profit-margin.s6t: A price below cost is a loss
profit-margin.s6b: Profit, margin, and markup are then negative. Do not send a negative margin to a form that asked for a discount percent. A discount is a cut from a list price, which is a different job.
profit-margin.diagram2: Margin divides by the price. Markup divides by the cost.

convert-base.name: How to convert a number between bases
convert-base.blurb: Convert one whole number between bases 2 and 36. 255 in base 10 is FF in base 16. No 0x prefix and no fraction.
convert-base.title: How to convert a number between bases
convert-base.lead: You have one integer in one base and you need another base. You will set both bases in this tab. This page does not turn letters into groups of 8 bits, and it does not accept a 0x prefix.
convert-base.result: The same integer written in the destination base, with letters in uppercase.
convert-base.note: Open the base converter when the integer and both bases are known. Bases are 2 through 36. Nothing is uploaded.
convert-base.s1t: Write the integer without a prefix
convert-base.s1b: 255 is a decimal integer. FF is hex. 11111111 is binary. Do not type 0x, 0b, or a dot. A fraction is a different job.
convert-base.s2t: Open the base converter on cv.cm
convert-base.s3t: Set the source base and the destination base
convert-base.s3b: Bases run from 2 to 36. Decimal to hex is 10 and 16. A digit must exist in the source base, so 2 is not a binary digit.
convert-base.s4b: A leading plus or minus is allowed. Letters may be upper or lower on input. The body can be at most 64 digits.
convert-base.s5b: 255 in base 10 is FF in base 16, and 11111111 in base 2. Zero stays 0. Copy is that integer, not a 0x prefix.
convert-base.s6b: A word such as hi is not an integer in base 16 unless every letter fits that base. The binary tool turns letters into 8-bit groups. This page converts one integer.
convert-base.diagram1: Bases 2–36. 255 decimal is FF hex. No 0x and no dot.
convert-base.diagram2: Output letters are uppercase. This page converts one integer.

add-duration.name: How to add hours and minutes
add-duration.blurb: Add or subtract two lengths written as hours:minutes:seconds. Minutes and seconds must be 0–59. 0:90:00 is not a valid length.
add-duration.title: How to add hours and minutes
add-duration.lead: You have two lengths of time, not two clock times. You will add them, or subtract the second from the first, in this tab. 1:30:00 plus 0:45:00 is 2:15:00. This is not a time zone.
add-duration.result: One length in H:MM:SS, plus the same length as a total number of seconds.
add-duration.note: Open time duration when both lengths are written as hours:minutes:seconds. Minutes and seconds must be 0–59. Nothing is uploaded.
add-duration.s1b: 1 hour 30 minutes is 1:30:00. 45 minutes is 0:45:00. 90 minutes is 1:30:00, not 0:90:00. Minutes and seconds above 59 fail.
add-duration.s2b: The math stays in this tab.
add-duration.s3b: Add joins the two lengths. Subtract takes the second away from the first. 1:30:00 minus 0:45:00 is 0:45:00.
add-duration.s4t: Read the clock-style result and the total seconds
add-duration.s4b: 1:30:00 plus 0:45:00 is 2:15:00, which is 8,100 seconds. Copy includes both lines. An API that wants seconds wants the second line.
add-duration.s5t: A longer second length makes a negative result
add-duration.s5b: 0:30:00 minus 0:45:00 is -0:15:00. The minus is a direction on a length. It is not a clock time before midnight.
add-duration.s6t: Keep this separate from a clock and a time zone
add-duration.s6b: 1:30:00 here is a length of 90 minutes. It is not 1:30 in the morning, and it does not move between New York and Shanghai.
add-duration.diagram2: A longer second length gives a minus. This is a length, not a clock.

calculate-percent.name: How to calculate a percentage
calculate-percent.blurb: Read four lines from the same two numbers. 25% of 200 is 50. 25 is 12.5% of 200. 200 plus 25% is 250.
calculate-percent.title: How to calculate a percentage
calculate-percent.lead: You have two numbers and four possible questions. You will enter them in this tab and copy the line that matches the question. 25% of 200, 25 as a percent of 200, and 200 increased by 25% are three different answers.
calculate-percent.result: The one line that matches the question: a percent of a number, what percent one number is of another, a number plus a percent, or the percent change from one number to the other.
calculate-percent.note: Open percentage when you can point at the two numbers. A zero in the second box leaves two of the lines as a dash. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-percent.s1t: Name which question you are answering
calculate-percent.s1b: 25% of 200 is 50. 25 is 12.5% of 200. 200 plus 25% is 250. The change from 200 to 25 is -87.5%. Copying the wrong line answers a different question.
calculate-percent.s2b: The four lines stay in this tab.
calculate-percent.s3t: Enter the two numbers in order
calculate-percent.s3b: The first box is the percent, or the part, or the new number, depending on the line. The second box is the whole, or the starting number. With 25 and 200, the first line is 25% of 200.
calculate-percent.s4t: Match the line to the question
calculate-percent.s4b: Percent of a number uses the first line. What percent one number is of another uses the second. A number plus a percent uses the third. The change from the second number to the first uses the fourth.
calculate-percent.s5t: A zero whole leaves two lines blank
calculate-percent.s5b: You cannot ask what percent something is of zero, and you cannot ask the percent change from zero. The first and third lines still run, because they do not divide by the second number.
calculate-percent.s6t: Copy only the line you named
calculate-percent.s6b: The clipboard gets all four lines. Paste the one that matches. 50, 12.5%, 250, and -87.5% must not be swapped.
calculate-percent.diagram1: 25 and 200: 50, 12.5%, 250, and -87.5% are four different answers.
calculate-percent.diagram2: Copy the line that matches the question. A zero whole blanks two lines.

days-between.name: How to count days between two dates
days-between.blurb: The signed difference does not include both ends. Monday 5 January 2026 to Friday 9 January is 4 days. The same span is 5 business days on the other page.
days-between.title: How to count days between two dates
days-between.lead: You need the calendar gap, not the weekday count. You will pick two civil dates in this tab. The same day is 0. Monday through Friday of one week is 4, because Friday is four midnights after Monday.
days-between.result: A signed day count, the absolute days, and the whole weeks left after dropping leftover days.
days-between.note: Open days between dates when you have two YYYY-MM-DD dates. This page does not skip weekends. Nothing is uploaded.
days-between.s1b: A hotel night from Monday to Friday is 4. A form that says “including both dates” wants 5. This page is the 4. The business-day page is a different count: it includes both ends and skips Saturday and Sunday.
days-between.s2t: Open days between dates on cv.cm
days-between.s2b: The count stays in this tab.
days-between.s3t: Pick the start and the end
days-between.s3b: Use calendar dates, not clock times. If the end is before the start, the signed count is negative. The absolute line stays zero or positive.
days-between.s4t: Read signed days, absolute days, and whole weeks
days-between.s4b: Whole weeks drop the leftover. 10 days is 1 whole week. 4 days is 0 whole weeks. Copy all three lines, then use the one the form named.
days-between.s5t: Count the leap day when it sits in the gap
days-between.s5b: 28 February 2024 to 1 March 2024 is 2 days, because 29 February is in the gap. 28 February 2023 to 1 March 2023 is 1 day.
days-between.s6b: Saturday and Sunday are ordinary calendar days here. If the form wants Monday through Friday only, use the business-day page and remember that page includes both ends.
days-between.diagram1: Mon 5 Jan to Fri 9 Jan 2026 is 4 days. Both ends are not included.
days-between.diagram2: 28 Feb 2024 to 1 Mar 2024 is 2 days. The leap day is in the gap.

shift-date.name: How to add days to a date
shift-date.blurb: Add a whole number of calendar days. 28 February 2024 plus 1 is 29 February 2024. A fraction of a day fails. Friday plus 1 is Saturday.
shift-date.title: How to add days to a date
shift-date.lead: You have a calendar date and a whole number of days. You will shift that date in this tab. Negative numbers go backward. The shift does not skip Saturday or Sunday.
shift-date.result: One new civil date, YYYY-MM-DD, after a whole number of calendar days.
shift-date.note: Open add days when the start date and the whole number are known. 1.5 days fails. Nothing is uploaded.
shift-date.s1t: Use a whole number of days
shift-date.s1b: 1 moves one calendar day. 1.5 is rejected. A negative number walks backward. This is not a business-day skip.
shift-date.s2b: The shift stays in this tab.
shift-date.s3b: Use a real civil date. 31 January plus 1 day is 1 February. The month length is already in the calendar.
shift-date.s4t: Let the leap day appear when the year has one
shift-date.s4b: 28 February 2024 plus 1 day is 29 February 2024. 28 February 2023 plus 1 day is 1 March 2023.
shift-date.s5t: Read the new date before you copy it
shift-date.s5b: Copy puts that YYYY-MM-DD on the clipboard. Check the year when the shift crosses 31 December.
shift-date.s6b: This page does not skip the weekend. If the form wants the next Monday after a Friday, add 3, or use the business-day page for a count that skips Saturday and Sunday.
shift-date.diagram2: A whole number only. Friday + 1 is Saturday.

iso-week.name: How to find the ISO week number
iso-week.blurb: ISO weeks start on Monday. Week 1 contains the year's first Thursday. 1 January 2021 is Friday of 2020-W53.
iso-week.title: How to find the ISO week number
iso-week.lead: You need the ISO week of a civil date. You will read the week label and the weekday in this tab. Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7. A date in late December can belong to next year's week 1.
iso-week.result: An ISO year, a week from 1 to 53, and a weekday from 1 to 7, with the label such as 2020-W53.
iso-week.note: Open week number when you have a civil date. This is not a week that starts on Sunday. Nothing is uploaded.
iso-week.s1t: Use the week that starts on Monday
iso-week.s1b: Monday is weekday 1. Sunday is weekday 7. A week number that starts on Sunday is a different system. This page will not produce that number.
iso-week.s2b: The week stays in this tab.
iso-week.s3b: The date is YYYY-MM-DD. Clock time does not move the week. 1 January 2026 is Thursday, weekday 4, and it is 2026-W01.
iso-week.s4t: Read the ISO year separately from the calendar year
iso-week.s4b: Week 1 is the week that contains the year's first Thursday. 1 January 2021 is a Friday, so it stays in 2020-W53. 30 December 2024 is a Monday in 2025-W01.
iso-week.s5t: Copy the label and the weekday
iso-week.s5b: The label looks like 2020-W53. The weekday is a number from 1 to 7. A spreadsheet that wants a Sunday-start week cannot use this label as-is.
iso-week.s6t: Check one Thursday you already know
iso-week.s6b: The first Thursday of the year is inside week 1. If 1 January is a Thursday, that date is weekday 4 of week 1 of the same year, as 2026-01-01 is 2026-W01.
iso-week.diagram1: Monday is 1. Sunday is 7. Week 1 holds the first Thursday.

vat-price.name: How to add VAT to a price
vat-price.blurb: Exclusive adds the tax. 100 at 20% becomes 120.00. Inclusive splits a gross price. 120 at 20% is 100.00 net and 20.00 tax, not 24.00.
vat-price.title: How to add VAT to a price
vat-price.lead: You have an amount and a rate you already chose. You will pick exclusive or inclusive in this tab. Exclusive adds tax to a net price. Inclusive takes tax out of a gross price. 120 times 20% is the wrong tax on a price that already includes 20%.
vat-price.result: Net, tax, and gross to two decimals, for the rate you typed.
vat-price.note: Open VAT when you know whether the amount already includes tax. The page does not look up a country rate. Nothing is uploaded.
vat-price.s1t: Say whether the amount already includes tax
vat-price.s1b: A net price uses exclusive. A shelf price that already includes tax uses inclusive. Mixing them changes the tax.
vat-price.s2b: The arithmetic stays in this tab.
vat-price.s3t: Type the amount and the rate you were given
vat-price.s3b: The rate is the number you type. This page does not choose 20% or 10% for a country. A negative amount or a negative rate fails.
vat-price.s4t: Add tax when the price is net
vat-price.s4b: Exclusive on 100 at 20% is net 100.00, tax 20.00, gross 120.00. Gross is the amount plus the tax.
vat-price.s5t: Split the price when tax is already inside
vat-price.s5b: Inclusive on 120 at 20% is net 100.00, tax 20.00, gross 120.00. Tax is not 120 times 20%. That product is 24.00, which is the tax you would add to a net 120.
vat-price.s6b: All three are two decimals. This is arithmetic on the numbers you typed. It is not a tax filing, and it does not name a currency.

percent-off.name: How to calculate a discount
percent-off.blurb: 20% off 100 is a sale price of 80.00 and a saving of 20.00. That is not a 20% profit margin. 120% off can go below zero.
percent-off.title: How to calculate a discount
